about: Worked examples of the WebSocket messages, with realistic values and a note on what each field holds. Every example is validated against protocol.schema.json by a test (crates/ce-protocol/tests/examples.rs), and docgen copies them into docs/PROTOCOL.md and docs/generated/asyncapi.json. Handles are made up.

subscribe.title: Start the live feed after the last event you have
subscribe.notes: `since` is the `seq` of the last `event` you received (the `cursor` of the snapshot on first connect). Omit it to get only new events.

contacts.list.title: Hostile contacts seen in chat, first 25
contacts.list.notes: `stance` filters on the decided stance (`kos` and `hostile` both count unless `exact`); `source` is where the player was seen; `requestId` comes back on the reply.

contacts.now.title: Who is near me now
contacts.now.notes: `view`: `here` (nearby in 15 minutes), `shared` (same shard, 2 hours) or `all`. Leave it out for the configured window.

contacts.tag.title: Mark a player hostile, with a note
contacts.tag.notes: A personal tag stays on this PC. `tag` is `kos`, `hostile`, `wary`, `neutral`, `friendly`, `ally` or `null` to clear it. `note` is free text up to 500 characters.

message.note: Pulled a gun at Port Tressler

contacts.category.title: How you know someone
contacts.category.notes: `category` is one of `my-org`, `org-affiliate`, `alliance`, `friend`, `frequent-party`, `mission-partner`, `encountered`, `stranger`, or `null` to go back to the Companion's own decision.

org.tag.title: An officer's org tag
org.tag.notes: Needs `admin` (a native client, or a page after `ce-companion approve`) and an officer role on the Hub. `org` is the SID the tag applies to; leave it out for your main org. The tag is shared with the org.

contact.delete.title: Delete a contact
contact.delete.notes: Needs `admin`. Removes the contact's rows and suppresses the name so it is not re-created.

truth.confirm.title: Confirm a commodity row with a corrected price
truth.confirm.notes: `rowIndex` counts from 0 in the terminal listing. Send `reviewRevision` from the queue item: a stale revision (the capture was reprocessed) is rejected. `values` holds only what you corrected; prices are whole aUEC per SCU.

sync.share.title: Share confirmed sightings and presence, not stock or blueprints
sync.share.notes: Needs `admin`. `sightings` is `off`, `confirmed` or `auto`; the others are on/off. Fields you leave out stay as they are.

blueprints.set.title: Say you have a blueprint the log did not report
blueprints.set.notes: `name` is the blueprint's name as the game shows it; the Companion matches it case-insensitively. `enabled: false` says you do not have it.

storage.cleanup.title: Preview the storage cleanup
storage.cleanup.notes: Needs `admin`. `dryRun: true` changes nothing and returns what would be reduced or expired.

auth.elevate.title: Ask for admin on this connection
auth.elevate.notes: The Companion answers with `auth.elevation` (a six-digit code); the user then runs `ce-companion approve <code>` on this PC.

error.title: A request failed
error.notes: `requestId` echoes the request, when it had one.

auth.required.title: The connection needs a higher scope
auth.required.notes: `for` is the message type that was refused and `scope` what it needs.

auth.elevation.title: Approve this on the PC
auth.elevation.notes: `code` is shown to the user, who runs `ce-companion approve <code>`. `connection` identifies this socket; `expiresInS` is how long the code is valid (120).

auth.scope.title: The connection holds admin for ten minutes

sync.status.title: Org sync set up and healthy
sync.status.notes: `pending` are outbox entries not yet sent, `rejected` those the Hub refused. `lastPullAt` and `lastPushAt` are ISO times. `role` is the Hub's view of you. `sharing` shows the four switches.

contact.deleted.title: A contact was deleted
contact.deleted.notes: `handleKey` is the lowercase handle, the key every contact table uses.

cz.timers.title: Two running timers
cz.timers.notes: `startedAt` is unix milliseconds; `key` names the timer.

background.state.title: Background work paused while the game is busy
background.state.notes: `waiting` is the number of queued jobs; `until` an ISO time when the hold ends, when known.
